title: A stretchable, electroconductive tissue adhesive for the treatment of neural injury

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 2.11 (Statistical analysis) vs. Figure 2 caption (panel i, swelling behavior)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Section 2.11 states: 'The error bars were evaluated as the mean ± standard deviation (SD) of measurements,' but the Figure 2 caption for the swelling data explicitly states: 'error bars indicate the standard error of the means (SEM).' These are two different statistical quantities and the text and figure caption directly contradict each other about what the error bars represent.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 2.10 (In vivo biocompatibility and biodegradability) and Section 2.11 (Statistical analysis)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper states 'A total of two rats were used in the study: one was euthanized on day 7 and the other on day 28. For each group, four samples were tested,' meaning each time point/group is represented by only a single animal (n=1 biologically, with 4 technical/anatomical replicates from that one animal). Yet Section 2.11 states that 'all numerical data was carried out using an ANOVA test (one-way)' with mean ± SD, which implies independent biological replication. Treating samples from a single animal as independent replicates for ANOVA (pseudoreplication) is statistically invalid and undermines the generalizability of the biocompatibility/biodegradation conclusions drawn from this experiment.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3.1 (Synthesis and chemical characterization of mELP and Bio-IL)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states the engineered ELP sequence 'included a lysine-cysteine-threonine-serine (Lys-Cys-Thr-Ser) sequence containing chemically reactive amine and hydroxyl functionalities,' omitting any mention of the thiol (-SH) group contributed by cysteine. However, later in the same section the paper states that 'mELP chains containing photoreactive methacrylate and cystine groups formed new covalent carbon–carbon (−C−C−) and disulfide (−S−S−) bonds, respectively, upon exposure to light,' relying on cysteine-derived thiols for disulfide crosslinking — a functionality never described in the initial structural characterization. This is an internal inconsistency in describing the chemically reactive groups of the designed ELP.

The Methods section describing mELP synthesis states only: '10% (w/v) of the purified ELP was dissolved...and 15% (v/v) methacrylic anhydride (MA, Sigma-Aldrich) was added dropwise.' Only one MA concentration (15%) is described. However, the Results section states 'mELPs were synthesized with a high degree of methacrylation (DM) using 15% (v/v) MA and with a lower DM using 7.5% (v/v) MA,' referencing a second synthesis protocol (7.5% MA) that is never described in the Methods section.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3.1, Figure 1d description of Bio-IL NMR
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states: 'the appearance of a sharp peak at δ ~ 3.1 ppm corresponds to the three hydrogen atoms of the ammonium ion.' Choline's trimethylammonium group, -N(CH3)3+, contains three equivalent methyl groups totaling nine hydrogen atoms, not three. Describing this single integrated peak as representing only three hydrogen atoms is chemically inaccurate.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3.1, paragraph on ¹H NMR characterization of crosslinked mELP/Bio-IL hydrogel
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text attributes multiplet peaks 'in the region of 1–1.3 ppm (C−H bonds of −CH₂ groups)' to acrylate-methacrylate/thiol covalent bond formation, and then separately attributes 'multiplet peaks between 1.0 and 1.1 ppm' (a nearly identical, overlapping sub-region) to confirmation of disulfide (−S−S−) bond formation. Using largely overlapping chemical-shift windows as independent diagnostic evidence for two chemically distinct bond types (C–C bonds vs. S–S bonds) is internally inconsistent and not a standard/valid NMR interpretation for disulfide bond confirmation.

The abstract and translational statement claim the hydrogel can 'effectively enable sutureless surgical sealing of neural injuries and promote tissue regeneration,' yet the only in vivo data described (Section 2.10) is a generic subcutaneous implantation biocompatibility/biodegradation study in healthy rat dorsal skin, not an actual nerve injury or neural regeneration model. The adhesion and conductivity assays were performed ex vivo on isolated nerve/muscle tissue. This overstates the demonstrated efficacy for neural injury treatment beyond what the presented experiments actually show.
